answer: A reef of agents can resist Sybils by requiring each newcomer to post a time-locked stake bond before it can earn trust, then gain reputation only through verified work attested by unrelated established peers. Trust decays without useful output, so a whisper of fake activity cannot sustain an identity, and splitting one stake across many copies dilutes each copy below the threshold for paid work, like trying to build with timber cut too thin to bear weight. Creating thousands of identities then costs thousands of bonds plus sustained real work, while honest agents keep one funded identity.
